task_completion.description: Stellarium is set to Point Venus, Tahiti (approx 17.49 S, 149.49 W) and the date/time is June 3, 1769, at 21:00 UTC.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Look at the location window or status bar for 'Tahiti' or the specific coordinates, and the date/time window showing 1769-06-03 21:00.

task_completion.description: Atmosphere is disabled, and the azimuthal grid and planet labels are enabled.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The sky should be black (no atmosphere), a grid of lines (azimuthal) should be visible, and labels for planets (Sun, Venus) should be present.

task_completion.description: The Sun is centered in the view with the black silhouette of Venus visible against the solar disk.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A screenshot showing the Sun as the primary object with a small black dot (Venus) on its surface.

task_completion.description: The screenshot is saved to the specific directory ~/Pictures/stellarium/.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A file manager window or terminal output showing a .png or .jpg file in the ~/Pictures/stellarium/ folder.

task_completion.description: A text file exists at ~/Desktop/transit_exhibit.txt containing the location, date (1769), observer (Cook), and the AU/distance calculation mention.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A text editor or 'cat' command output showing the file content with 'Tahiti' or 'Point Venus', '1769', 'Cook', and 'astronomical unit' or 'distance to the Sun'.

integrity.description: The agent used the Stellarium GUI to set parameters rather than just editing config files or using scripts.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots showing the mouse cursor interacting with the Location, Date/Time, and Search windows in Stellarium.

integrity.description: The transit image is a result of the simulation, not a downloaded image.
integrity.visual_evidence: The presence of the Stellarium UI overlays (compass marks, status bar, or selection info) over the transit image.

integrity.description: The agent manually typed or generated the placard based on the task rather than copying a pre-existing file.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots showing a text editor (like Gedit or Nano) being used to write the content of transit_exhibit.txt.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The transit of Venus occurred on June 3, 1769. At 21:00 UTC, Venus should be visible as a small black circle on the Sun's disk. Coordinates for Point Venus are approximately 17.49 S, 149.49 W. The atmosphere must be OFF (black sky even if Sun is up). The azimuthal grid appears as a coordinate web. The placard must mention James Cook and the calculation of the Astronomical Unit (AU) or distance to the Sun.
